questions.q: Who is Yahweh who makes this declaration concerning Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh is the one who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will make Jerusalem like for all the surrounding peoples?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will make Jerusalem like a strong drink that makes all the surrounding peoples stagger.

questions.q: Who is going to gather against Jerusalem?
questions.a: All the nations of the earth are going to gather against Jerusalem.

questions.q: On the day when all the nations gather against Judah, what specific things did Yahweh say he would do to the horses and riders of the enemy armies?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would strike every horse with confusion and each rider with madness. Yahweh also said he would strike every horse of the enemy nations with blindness.

questions.q: What will the leaders of Judah say about the people of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The leaders of Judah will say that the people of Jerusalem are a strength to them through Yahweh of Armies, their God.

questions.q: In that day, what will the leaders of Judah be like?
questions.a: In that day, the leaders of Judah will be like a basin of fire among trees and like a torch of fire in a sheaf.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh save the tents of Judah first?
questions.a: Yahweh will save the tents of Judah first so that the honor of the house of David and the honor of those who live in Jerusalem may not be greater than the rest of Judah.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he will do for the people of Jerusalem on that day?
questions.a: Yahweh said he will defend the people of Jerusalem, and even the weakest among them will become as strong as David.

questions.q: What is Yahweh determined to do on that day?
questions.a: Yahweh said that on that day he is determined to destroy all the nations who come against Jerusalem.

questions.q: On that day, what will Yahweh pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh will pour out a spirit of favor and supplications.

questions.q: What will the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem do when they look upon him whom they have pierced?
questions.a: When they look on him whom they have pierced, they will lament and mourn for him as one mourns and laments for an only son or over the death of a firstborn son.

questions.q: What will the mourning in Jerusalem be like on that day?
questions.a: The mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.

questions.q: How will the land mourn in that day?
questions.a: The land will mourn by clans: each clan will mourn separately, and within each clan, the men and their wives will mourn separately from each other.

commentary.text: Punishment of the enemies of Judah.
Repentance and sorrow of the Jews.

Verses 1–8 Here is a Divine prediction, which will be a heavy burden to all the enemies of the church. But it is for Israel; for their comfort and benefit. It is promised that God will make foolish the counsels, and weaken the courage of the enemies of the church. The exact meaning is not clear; but God often begins by calling the poor and despised; and in that day even the feeblest will resemble David, and be as eminent in courage and every thing good. Desirable indeed is it that the examples and labours of Christians should render them as fire among wood, as a torch in a sheaf, to kindle the flame of Divine love, to spread religion on the right hand and on the left.

The day here spoken of, is the day of Jerusalem's defence and deliverance, that glorious day when God will appear for the salvation of his people. In Christ's first coming he bruised the serpent's head, and broke all the powers of darkness that fought against God's kingdom among men. In his second coming he will complete their destruction, when he shall put down all opposing rule, principality, and power; and death itself shall be swallowed up in that victory. The Holy Spirit is gracious and merciful, and is the Author of all grace or holiness. He, also, is the Spirit of supplications, and shows men their ignorance, want, guilt, misery, and danger. At the time here foretold, the Jews will know who the crucified Jesus was; then they shall look by faith to him, and mourn with the deepest sorrow, not only in public, but in private, even each one separately. There is a holy mourning, the effect of the pouring out of the Spirit; a mourning for sin, which quickens faith in Christ, and qualifies for joy in God. This mourning is a fruit of the Spirit of grace, a proof of a work of grace in the soul, and of the Spirit of supplications. It is fulfilled in all who sorrow for sin after a godly sort; they look to Christ crucified, and mourn for him. Looking by faith upon the cross of Christ will cause us to mourn for sin after a godly sort.
